01-01.title: Lincoln issues the Emancipation Proclamation
01-01.summary: On the third winter of the American Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln declared all enslaved people in the rebelling Confederate states to be free, reframing the war as a moral fight against slavery.

01-03.title: Pope Leo X excommunicates Martin Luther
01-03.summary: Three years after Luther nailed his Ninety-Five Theses to a church door in Wittenberg, the papal bull Decet Romanum Pontificem formally cast him out of the Catholic Church and accelerated the Protestant Reformation.

01-04.title: Isaac Newton is born in Woolsthorpe, England
01-04.summary: The mathematician whose laws of motion and theory of universal gravitation would underpin classical physics for the next two and a half centuries was born on Christmas Day under the old Julian calendar.

01-08.title: Andrew Jackson wins the Battle of New Orleans
01-08.summary: Two weeks after a peace treaty had already ended the War of 1812, US forces routed a much larger British army outside New Orleans, making Jackson a national hero and reshaping American politics.

01-15.title: Martin Luther King Jr. is born in Atlanta
01-15.summary: The Baptist minister who would lead the American civil rights movement, deliver the 'I Have a Dream' speech and win the Nobel Peace Prize at thirty-five was born in segregated Georgia.

01-17.title: Captain Cook crosses the Antarctic Circle
01-17.summary: HMS Resolution became the first European ship to cross the Antarctic Circle, though pack ice forced James Cook to turn back before sighting the continent itself.

01-20.title: Iran releases 52 American hostages after 444 days
01-20.summary: Minutes after Ronald Reagan was sworn in as the 40th US president, Tehran freed the embassy staff it had held since the 1979 revolution, ending the crisis that had crippled the Carter administration.

01-21.title: Louis XVI is guillotined in Paris
01-21.summary: The deposed king of France was beheaded at the Place de la Révolution before a crowd of 20,000, an act of regicide that horrified Europe and pushed the French Revolution into its bloodiest phase.

01-24.title: Gold is discovered at Sutter's Mill in California
01-24.summary: James W. Marshall spotted flakes of gold in the tailrace of a sawmill on the American River, touching off a stampede that drew 300,000 people to California and reshaped the American West.

01-27.title: Soviet troops liberate Auschwitz
01-27.summary: The Red Army's 322nd Rifle Division reached the largest Nazi extermination camp in occupied Poland, where more than a million people had been murdered. The date is now observed as International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

01-28.title: The space shuttle Challenger breaks apart 73 seconds into flight
01-28.summary: An O-ring seal in a solid rocket booster failed after liftoff from Kennedy Space Center, killing all seven crew members including teacher Christa McAuliffe and halting US human spaceflight for nearly three years.

01-30.title: Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated in New Delhi
01-30.summary: On his way to evening prayers, the architect of Indian independence was shot three times by Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist who blamed him for accommodating Pakistan during the bloody 1947 partition.

02-02.title: German Sixth Army surrenders at Stalingrad
02-02.summary: After five months of urban warfare in temperatures below minus 30°C, Field Marshal Friedrich Paulus surrendered the remnants of his 91,000-strong force to the Red Army, marking the turning point of the war on the Eastern Front.

02-04.title: George Washington is unanimously elected first US president
02-04.summary: Every elector in the new United States cast a vote for the Virginia general, the only president ever chosen unanimously. He took office two months later in New York City.

02-09.title: The Beatles debut on The Ed Sullivan Show
02-09.summary: Seventy-three million Americans, roughly two-fifths of the country, watched the four young men from Liverpool play 'All My Loving' and four other songs, igniting the British Invasion of US popular music.

02-11.title: Nelson Mandela walks free after 27 years in prison
02-11.summary: The future South African president stepped through the gates of Victor Verster Prison hand in hand with his wife Winnie, four years before he would defeat F.W. de Klerk in the country's first multi-racial election.

02-12.title: Charles Darwin and Abraham Lincoln are both born
02-12.summary: By coincidence, the English naturalist who would propose the theory of evolution by natural selection and the American statesman who would emancipate four million slaves were born on the same day.

02-14.title: The St. Valentine's Day Massacre
02-14.summary: Seven members of Bugs Moran's North Side Gang were lined up against a garage wall in Chicago and gunned down with submachine guns by men dressed as police officers, a hit widely attributed to Al Capone.

02-15.title: USS Maine explodes in Havana harbor
02-15.summary: An unexplained explosion sank the American battleship and killed 260 sailors. 'Remember the Maine!' became the rallying cry that pushed a reluctant United States into war with Spain three months later.

02-22.title: The Miracle on Ice at Lake Placid
02-22.summary: A US Olympic ice hockey team of college students upset the heavily favored Soviet squad, four-time defending gold medalists, 4–3 in a semifinal at the Winter Games. The Americans went on to take gold two days later.

02-27.title: The Reichstag in Berlin burns
02-27.summary: Fire gutted the German parliament building four weeks after Hitler became chancellor. Blaming the Communists, the Nazis used the blaze to push through emergency decrees that suspended civil liberties and consolidated their dictatorship.

03-04.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt is inaugurated amid the Great Depression
03-04.summary: Taking office with a quarter of the workforce unemployed and banks closed across the country, FDR told Americans that 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself' and launched the New Deal within his first hundred days.

03-05.title: Joseph Stalin dies in Moscow
03-05.summary: The Soviet leader who had ruled with an iron grip for nearly three decades died of a stroke at his dacha at age 74. His death triggered a power struggle that Nikita Khrushchev eventually won, leading to a partial 'de-Stalinization'.

03-10.title: Alexander Graham Bell makes the first telephone call
03-10.summary: From a Boston laboratory, Bell called out to his assistant in the next room: 'Mr. Watson — come here — I want to see you.' Within five years his patent had spawned a network of 50,000 telephones across the United States.

03-11.title: Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami devastate Japan
03-11.summary: A magnitude 9.1 quake off the Pacific coast sent a 40-meter tsunami over coastal communities, killing nearly 20,000 people and triggering meltdowns at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant.

03-14.title: Albert Einstein is born in Ulm, Germany
03-14.summary: The patent clerk who would publish four world-changing papers in 1905 alone — on the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity and mass-energy equivalence — was born to a secular Jewish family in the Kingdom of Württemberg.

03-15.title: Julius Caesar is assassinated on the Ides of March
03-15.summary: Stabbed 23 times by a group of senators including his protégé Marcus Brutus, the Roman dictator collapsed at the foot of a statue of his rival Pompey. His death triggered another civil war that ended the Roman Republic.

03-17.title: Saint Patrick dies in Ireland
03-17.summary: The Romano-British missionary who, captured as a slave at sixteen and later returning to spread Christianity, became the patron saint of Ireland died on this date around the year 461. His feast has been a holiday in Ireland since the 17th century.

03-20.title: The United States invades Iraq
03-20.summary: After Saddam Hussein refused to leave Baghdad, US-led 'coalition of the willing' forces crossed the Kuwaiti border and began the war that would topple the regime within three weeks and destabilize the region for years.

03-23.title: Patrick Henry gives the 'Give me liberty, or give me death!' speech
03-23.summary: Before the Second Virginia Convention in Richmond, the firebrand lawyer urged armed resistance to British rule. The convention voted to mobilize the colony's militia, putting Virginia on the road to revolution.

04-04.title: Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated in Memphis
04-04.summary: The civil rights leader was shot on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel, where he had come to support striking sanitation workers. James Earl Ray was arrested two months later in London and confessed.

04-06.title: The United States enters the First World War
04-06.summary: Two months after Germany resumed unrestricted submarine warfare against neutral shipping, Congress declared war and committed the country to fighting on the Allied side, sending two million doughboys to Europe by war's end.

04-11.title: Apollo 13 launches toward the Moon
04-11.summary: James Lovell's crew lifted off from Kennedy Space Center for what would become NASA's most-watched failure. An oxygen tank rupture two days later forced an improvised return to Earth that the world followed live on television.

04-12.title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
04-12.summary: The 27-year-old Soviet cosmonaut orbited Earth once aboard Vostok 1, parachuting from the capsule and landing in a field near the Volga River 108 minutes after liftoff. He became an instant international celebrity.

04-14.title: RMS Titanic strikes an iceberg in the North Atlantic
04-14.summary: Four days into her maiden voyage from Southampton to New York, the British ocean liner — billed as practically unsinkable — sideswiped an iceberg at 11:40 pm and went down before dawn, drowning more than 1,500 people.

04-15.title: Abraham Lincoln dies from his assassin's bullet
04-15.summary: Shot the previous evening by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre in Washington, the 16th president died across the street at the Petersen House at 7:22 am. He was the first US president to be assassinated.

04-18.title: Paul Revere rides through the Massachusetts night
04-18.summary: The Boston silversmith galloped to Lexington to warn Samuel Adams and John Hancock that British regulars were marching to seize colonial weapons, setting up the next day's battles at Lexington and Concord that began the American Revolution.

04-19.title: Bombing of the Oklahoma City federal building
04-19.summary: A truck bomb planted by anti-government extremist Timothy McVeigh destroyed the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building, killing 168 people including 19 children at a day-care center inside. It was the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in US history.

04-26.title: Reactor No. 4 explodes at Chernobyl
04-26.summary: A botched safety test at the Soviet nuclear power plant in northern Ukraine sent a plume of radioactive material across Europe, contaminated an exclusion zone larger than Luxembourg, and accelerated calls for political reform that would help unravel the USSR.

04-30.title: Hitler commits suicide in his Berlin bunker
04-30.summary: With Soviet troops blocks away, Adolf Hitler shot himself and his new wife Eva Braun took cyanide in the Führerbunker beneath the Reich Chancellery. Germany's unconditional surrender followed eight days later.

05-01.title: The Empire State Building opens in New York
05-01.summary: President Herbert Hoover pressed a button in Washington to switch on the lights of the world's tallest building, a 102-story Art Deco skyscraper built in just thirteen months at the height of the Depression.

05-06.title: The Hindenburg airship bursts into flames at Lakehurst
05-06.summary: The German passenger zeppelin caught fire while attempting to dock at the New Jersey naval air station, killing 36 people and ending the era of commercial airship travel. A radio reporter's anguished cry — 'Oh, the humanity!' — was recorded live.

05-07.title: Germany signs unconditional surrender at Reims
05-07.summary: In a small red-brick schoolhouse serving as Eisenhower's headquarters, General Alfred Jodl signed papers ending six years of war in Europe. The cessation of hostilities took effect just before midnight the following day.

05-08.title: Victory in Europe Day
05-08.summary: Crowds celebrated in cities across the Allied world as the German surrender signed the previous day formally took effect. Winston Churchill addressed jubilant Londoners from the Ministry of Health balcony in Whitehall.

05-14.title: The State of Israel is proclaimed in Tel Aviv
05-14.summary: Hours before the British Mandate for Palestine expired, David Ben-Gurion declared the establishment of a Jewish state. The United States recognized it within minutes; five Arab armies invaded the following day.

05-17.title: Brown v. Board of Education is decided
05-17.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled unanimously that racially segregated public schools were unconstitutional, overturning the 'separate but equal' doctrine that had stood since 1896 and launching the modern civil rights movement.

05-29.title: Hillary and Tenzing reach the summit of Mount Everest
05-29.summary: Edmund Hillary, a New Zealand beekeeper, and Tenzing Norgay, a Nepalese Sherpa, became the first climbers confirmed to stand on the world's highest point. News reached Britain four days later, on the morning of Queen Elizabeth II's coronation.

06-04.title: The Chinese army clears Tiananmen Square
06-04.summary: After seven weeks of student-led protests calling for democratic reform, the People's Liberation Army moved into central Beijing with tanks and live ammunition, killing hundreds — possibly thousands — of demonstrators and bystanders.

06-06.title: Allied forces land in Normandy on D-Day
06-06.summary: The largest seaborne invasion in history put 156,000 American, British and Canadian troops ashore on five French beaches. By month's end the Allies had a million men in Normandy and the liberation of Western Europe was underway.

06-12.title: Anne Frank receives the diary that will make her famous
06-12.summary: On her thirteenth birthday, the German-Jewish girl was given a red-checked autograph book by her parents in Amsterdam. She began writing in it that day; her family went into hiding from the Nazis three weeks later.

06-14.title: The Continental Congress adopts the Stars and Stripes
06-14.summary: Meeting in Philadelphia, the Congress resolved that the flag of the new United States would have thirteen alternating red and white stripes and thirteen white stars on a blue field, 'representing a new constellation'.

06-18.title: Napoleon is defeated at Waterloo
06-18.summary: An Anglo-allied army under the Duke of Wellington and a Prussian force under Field Marshal Blücher combined to break the French emperor's army outside Brussels, ending his 'Hundred Days' return from exile and his career.

06-25.title: North Korea invades South Korea
06-25.summary: Seven divisions of the Korean People's Army crossed the 38th parallel at dawn, beginning a three-year war that drew in the United Nations, the People's Republic of China and the Soviet Union and still has not formally ended.

06-28.title: Archduke Franz Ferdinand is assassinated in Sarajevo
06-28.summary: Gavrilo Princip, a 19-year-old Bosnian Serb nationalist, shot the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne and his wife Sophie at point-blank range. The killing set off the diplomatic crisis that led to the First World War six weeks later.

07-01.title: The Battle of the Somme begins
07-01.summary: British forces suffered 57,470 casualties — including 19,240 dead — in a single day, the worst in their army's history. The offensive ground on for four and a half months and produced more than a million combined casualties.

07-04.title: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence
07-04.summary: Meeting in Philadelphia, delegates from the thirteen colonies approved Thomas Jefferson's text declaring themselves 'free and independent states' and severed political ties with Great Britain. The date became the United States' national holiday.

07-14.title: Parisians storm the Bastille
07-14.summary: A crowd seeking arms and gunpowder besieged and captured the medieval fortress-prison on the eastern edge of Paris, killing its governor. The fall of the Bastille became the symbolic start of the French Revolution.

07-16.title: The Trinity nuclear test in the New Mexico desert
07-16.summary: Scientists of the Manhattan Project detonated the first atomic device at the Alamogordo Bombing Range. Robert Oppenheimer later recalled a verse from the Bhagavad Gita: 'Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.'

07-20.title: Apollo 11 lands two men on the Moon
07-20.summary: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin set the lunar module Eagle down in the Sea of Tranquility while Michael Collins orbited overhead. Six hours later Armstrong stepped onto the surface — 'one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind.'

07-22.title: John Dillinger is killed outside Chicago's Biograph Theater
07-22.summary: FBI agents shot the bank-robbing celebrity gangster as he left a screening of Manhattan Melodrama. His death came thirteen months after he led the daring escape from an Indiana jail that made him 'Public Enemy No. 1'.

07-29.title: Charles and Diana marry at St Paul's Cathedral
07-29.summary: An estimated 750 million people in 74 countries watched the heir to the British throne wed 20-year-old Lady Diana Spencer in a televised ceremony declared by the Archbishop of Canterbury as 'the stuff of which fairy tales are made'.

08-06.title: The atomic bombing of Hiroshima
08-06.summary: The B-29 Enola Gay dropped a uranium bomb on the Japanese city of Hiroshima, killing an estimated 70,000 people instantly and a similar number from injuries and radiation in the months that followed. Nagasaki was bombed three days later.

08-09.title: Nagasaki is destroyed by a plutonium bomb
08-09.summary: Three days after Hiroshima, the bomber Bockscar dropped a second atomic weapon on the Japanese port city of Nagasaki, killing around 40,000 people immediately. Japan announced its surrender six days later, ending the Second World War.

08-13.title: East Germany begins building the Berlin Wall
08-13.summary: Under cover of darkness, East German troops and police strung barbed wire down the 43-kilometer border between East and West Berlin. Within months it had become a concrete wall that would divide the city for 28 years.

08-15.title: India and Pakistan gain independence from Britain
08-15.summary: At midnight, two new sovereign states emerged from the partitioned British Raj. The hurried division along religious lines triggered one of the largest mass migrations in human history, with violence that killed up to two million people.

08-17.title: Woodstock — Janis Joplin and The Who close night two
08-17.summary: On Saturday night of the upstate New York music festival, more than 400,000 people watched Joplin, Creedence Clearwater Revival, The Grateful Dead, Sly and the Family Stone, and The Who in a marathon set that ran past dawn. Woodstock became the defining event of the 1960s counterculture.

08-16.title: Elvis Presley dies at Graceland
08-16.summary: The 42-year-old singer was found unresponsive on his bathroom floor at his Memphis estate; the cause of death was given as cardiac arrhythmia. An estimated 80,000 people lined the streets the day of his funeral.

08-19.title: Hardline Soviet officials attempt a coup against Mikhail Gorbachev
08-19.summary: Eight senior figures detained the Soviet leader at his Crimean dacha and tried to halt his reforms by sending tanks into Moscow. The coup collapsed within three days when Boris Yeltsin rallied resistance outside the Russian parliament.

08-28.title: 'I Have a Dream' delivered at the Lincoln Memorial
08-28.summary: Speaking to 250,000 people gathered for the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom, Martin Luther King Jr. departed from his prepared text and improvised the most famous oration of the American civil rights movement.

08-29.title: Hurricane Katrina makes landfall on the Gulf Coast
08-29.summary: The Category 3 storm overwhelmed the levees protecting New Orleans, flooding 80% of the city and exposing failures at every level of government. More than 1,800 people died, most of them in Louisiana.

09-02.title: Japan signs the formal surrender on USS Missouri
09-02.summary: Aboard the American battleship anchored in Tokyo Bay, foreign minister Mamoru Shigemitsu signed the Instrument of Surrender as General Douglas MacArthur looked on, ending the Second World War.

09-09.title: Mao Zedong dies in Beijing
09-09.summary: The 82-year-old founder of the People's Republic of China died after a long illness, ending 27 years at the helm of the Chinese Communist Party. His death cleared the way for Deng Xiaoping's market reforms.

09-11.title: Hijacked airliners destroy the World Trade Center
09-11.summary: Nineteen al-Qaeda operatives commandeered four passenger jets, flying two into the Twin Towers in New York and one into the Pentagon. The fourth, United 93, crashed in a Pennsylvania field after passengers fought back. Nearly 3,000 people died.

09-15.title: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
09-15.summary: The 158-year-old American investment bank collapsed with $619 billion in debt, the largest bankruptcy filing in US history and the moment the global financial crisis turned from worry to panic.

10-04.title: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1
10-04.summary: A 58-centimeter aluminum sphere with four trailing antennas became the first artificial Earth satellite, beeping out a radio signal from low orbit and shocking the United States into a frantic catch-up that birthed NASA.

10-12.title: Columbus makes landfall in the Bahamas
10-12.summary: After thirty-three days at sea, the Genoese navigator commanding three Spanish ships sighted an island he named San Salvador. The voyage, intended to find a westward route to Asia, opened sustained contact between Europe and the Americas.

10-14.title: William the Conqueror wins the Battle of Hastings
10-14.summary: The Norman duke defeated King Harold II of England, killed by an arrow to the eye according to the Bayeux Tapestry. Within ten weeks William was crowned king at Westminster Abbey, beginning the Norman conquest of England.

10-22.title: Kennedy reveals Soviet missiles in Cuba
10-22.summary: In a televised address, President John F. Kennedy informed Americans that the USSR had installed nuclear weapons 90 miles from Florida and announced a naval 'quarantine' of the island, opening the thirteen-day Cuban Missile Crisis.

10-29.title: Black Tuesday on Wall Street
10-29.summary: A record 16 million shares changed hands on the New York Stock Exchange as panic selling wiped out roughly $14 billion in market value in a single day, the climactic crash of an autumn collapse that ushered in the Great Depression.

10-31.title: Martin Luther posts the Ninety-Five Theses
10-31.summary: The Augustinian friar sent his Latin objections to the sale of indulgences to the Archbishop of Mainz, and — by tradition — nailed a copy to the door of All Saints' Church in Wittenberg. The act is conventionally taken as the start of the Protestant Reformation.

11-09.title: The Berlin Wall falls
11-09.summary: An East German official mistakenly announced at a press conference that border restrictions were lifted 'immediately'. Crowds gathered at checkpoints; overwhelmed guards opened the gates, and Berliners on both sides chipped away at the wall with hammers through the night.

11-11.title: Armistice ends the fighting on the Western Front
11-11.summary: At the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month, the guns fell silent in a railway carriage in the Forest of Compiègne. The First World War left at least 17 million dead and reshaped the political map of Europe.

11-19.title: Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address
11-19.summary: At the dedication of a national cemetery on the Pennsylvania battlefield, the president spoke for just two minutes — 272 words about a nation 'conceived in liberty' — and produced one of the most quoted speeches in American history.

11-22.title: John F. Kennedy is assassinated in Dallas
11-22.summary: The 35th president was shot in the head while riding in a presidential motorcade through Dealey Plaza. Lee Harvey Oswald was arrested within ninety minutes and murdered two days later by nightclub owner Jack Ruby.

12-01.title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her seat in Montgomery
12-01.summary: The 42-year-old seamstress was arrested for violating Alabama segregation laws when she would not move to the back of a city bus. Her arrest triggered a year-long boycott that propelled a young pastor named Martin Luther King Jr. to national prominence.

12-07.title: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
12-07.summary: A surprise carrier-launched raid on the US Pacific Fleet's base in Hawaii killed 2,403 Americans, sank or damaged nineteen ships, and brought the United States into the Second World War the next day with President Roosevelt's 'date which will live in infamy' speech.

12-10.title: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is adopted
12-10.summary: Drafted under the chairmanship of Eleanor Roosevelt, the document was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris with 48 states in favor and eight abstentions. It became the foundation of modern international human rights law.

12-17.title: The Wright brothers achieve powered flight
12-17.summary: On the dunes at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright piloted a homemade biplane through 120 feet of air in 12 seconds. Three further flights that day demonstrated the principle of heavier-than-air controlled human flight.

12-25.title: Charlemagne is crowned Holy Roman Emperor
12-25.summary: Pope Leo III placed an imperial crown on the Frankish king's head during Christmas Mass at Old St Peter's Basilica in Rome, reviving the title of Western emperor that had lapsed when the last Roman emperor in the West was deposed in 476.

12-26.title: Indian Ocean tsunami kills more than 230,000
12-26.summary: A magnitude 9.1 undersea earthquake off Sumatra sent walls of water crashing onto coastlines from Indonesia to East Africa. It was the deadliest tsunami in recorded history and one of the worst natural disasters ever documented.

12-31.title: Boris Yeltsin resigns as Russian president
12-31.summary: Hours before midnight Moscow time, the ailing first president of post-Soviet Russia announced his retirement in a televised address and handed the office to his hand-picked successor, Vladimir Putin, the acting prime minister.
